newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Jan 23.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp and Ford Motor Co have agreed to share engines to cut development costs. Under the agreement, Mazda will develop engines for small vehicles and Ford for larger models. The first engine Mazda will develop is an in-line four-cylinder model with a displacement of 1800-2000 cc. It will be used to power a recreational vehicle expected to be produced by Ford in the United States from 1999. They hope to sell about 300,000 of the vehicles in Japan annually under Mazda's brand name.

Sapporo Breweries Ltd plans to spend 23.3 billion yen to boost production of canned and draft beer in kegs, and to increase brewing capacity at its seven plants in Japan. Sapporo wants to increase canned beer production at its 10 plants by 17 percent to 194,000 cases per day.

Sony Music Entertainment (Japan) Inc is expected to increase its consolidated net profit by 39 percent to 14 billion yen in the business year to March, helped by strong sales of PlayStation game machines by Sony Computer Entertainment Inc.

Two specialty steel makers -- Daido Steel Co Ltd and Aichi Steel Works Ltd -- are expected to see their pre-tax profits rise in the year to March, thanks to increased car output. But Sanyo Special Steel Co Ltd and Hitachi Metals Ltd are expected to see lower profits due to lower product prices. Mitsubishi Steel Mfg Co Ltd is expected to trim its pre-tax loss to five billion yen, compared with 11.4 billion yen the year before.
